# Ticket 1 — Remember, list and forget Claude accounts — Round 1

### Blocked by
—

### Description
T3 can remember the Claude account that is currently logged in on one of its Claude setups, under a name the user chooses, show which accounts it remembers and which account is active on each Claude setup, and forget a remembered account again. Several accounts can be remembered per machine. The remembered login is kept in T3's own secret storage with the same protection as T3's other secrets and never appears in a listing, an error, or a log. Forgetting never touches a setup: an account that is still logged in stays logged in.

This ticket builds the backend service only. Nothing calls it from a client yet (a later frontend Auftrag does that), and switching between accounts is ticket 2 and ticket 3. On any system other than Linux, all three actions answer that they are unavailable.

A "Claude setup" is a configured Claude provider instance (driver kind `claudeAgent`), addressed by its `ProviderInstanceId`.

### Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario AK-1: Remember the account logged in on a setup under a chosen name
  Given a Claude setup on which the account "alice@example.com" is logged in
  And T3 remembers no accounts yet
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then T3 remembers one account named "Work" for "alice@example.com"
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-2: Several accounts can be remembered on one machine
  Given T3 remembers the account "alice@example.com" under the name "Work"
  And a second Claude setup on which "bob@example.com" is logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember the second setup's account under the name "Private"
  Then T3 remembers both "Work" and "Private"
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-3: Remembering is refused when no account is logged in
  Given a Claude setup on which no account is logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then the request is refused with the reason that no account is logged in on this setup
  And T3 remembers no new account
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-4: Remembering under a name already in use is refused
  Given T3 remembers "alice@example.com" under the name "Work"
  And a Claude setup on which "bob@example.com" is logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then the request is refused with the reason that the name "Work" is already in use
  And "Work" still stands for "alice@example.com"
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-5: List shows remembered accounts and the active account per setup
  Given T3 remembers "Work" for "alice@example.com" and "Private" for "bob@example.com"
  And setup one has "alice@example.com" logged in and setup two has "bob@example.com" logged in
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer names "Work" and "Private"
  And it shows "Work" as active on setup one and "Private" as active on setup two
Serves: R2

Scenario AK-6: List shows an active account that is not remembered
  Given a Claude setup on which "carol@example.com" is logged in
  And T3 does not remember "carol@example.com"
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer shows "carol@example.com" as active on that setup
  And it marks that account as not remembered
Serves: R2

Scenario AK-7: List with nothing remembered
  Given T3 remembers no accounts
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer contains no remembered accounts
  And it still shows which account is active on each Claude setup
Serves: R2

Scenario AK-8: Forget an account that is not active
  Given T3 remembers "Work" and "Private"
  And no Claude setup has the "Private" account active
  When T3 is asked to forget "Private"
  Then T3 remembers only "Work"
Serves: R3

Scenario AK-9: Forgetting the active account keeps the setup logged in
  Given a Claude setup with "alice@example.com" logged in, remembered as "Work"
  When T3 is asked to forget "Work"
  Then T3 no longer remembers "Work"
  And the setup is still logged in as "alice@example.com"
  And a new turn in a thread on that setup runs as "alice@example.com"
Serves: R3

Scenario AK-23: Remembered logins are kept in T3's protected secret storage
  Given a Claude setup with "alice@example.com" logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then the saved login is kept with the same protection as T3's other secrets
  And it cannot be found in plain form anywhere else in T3's own data
Serves: R11

Scenario AK-24: The account list never reveals a login
  Given T3 remembers "Work" and "Private"
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer contains names, account identities and which one is active
  And it contains no part of any saved login
Serves: R11

Scenario AK-27: Remembering is unavailable outside Linux
  Given a T3 server running on a system other than Linux
  When T3 is asked to remember a setup's account
  Then the answer says the action is unavailable on this system
  And nothing is remembered
Serves: R13

Scenario AK-28: Listing is unavailable outside Linux
  Given a T3 server running on a system other than Linux
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer says the action is unavailable on this system
Serves: R13

Scenario AK-29: Forgetting is unavailable outside Linux
  Given a T3 server running on a system other than Linux
  When T3 is asked to forget a remembered account
  Then the answer says the action is unavailable on this system
Serves: R13
```

### Test specification
All tests use setups whose Claude config directory is a temporary directory the test creates and removes; no test reads or writes `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json` or `~/.t3` (guard rail). Each setup is declared through `ServerSettingsService.layerTest({ providerInstances: { <id>: { driver: "claudeAgent", config: { homePath: <tmp dir> } } } })`, and its login is written by the test as two fixture files: `<tmp>/.credentials.json` = `{ "claudeAiOauth": { "accessToken": "<unique token>", "refreshToken": "<unique token>", "expiresAt": <ms>, "scopes": ["user:inference"] }, "mcpOAuth": { … } }` and `<tmp>/.claude.json` = `{ "oauthAccount": { "emailAddress": "alice@example.com", "accountUuid": "<uuid>", "organizationUuid": "<uuid>" }, "numStartups": 3, "projects": { … } }`. Token fixture values are unique random strings so a leak search cannot match by accident.

Unit (`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.test.ts`, extended):
- `resolveClaudeSetupPaths` with a configured `homePath` returns that directory and `<dir>/.claude.json`.
- With an empty `homePath` and an inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, it returns the inherited directory and `<inherited>/.claude.json`.
- With an empty `homePath` and no inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, it returns `<home>/.claude` and `<home>/.claude.json` (with `HostProcess.HomeDirectory` provided as a temp path; nothing is read from disk).

Integration (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts`, through the `ClaudeAccounts` service, real `ServerSecretStore` over `ServerConfig.layerTest(process.cwd(), { prefix: "t3-claude-accounts-test-" })`, real `FileSystem`/`Path`, `HostProcess.Platform` provided as `"linux"` unless stated):
- AK-1: remember `{ instanceId: setupOne, name: "Work" }` on a logged-in setup returns `{ name: "Work", email: "alice@example.com" }`, and `list` then has exactly one account `{ name: "Work", email: "alice@example.com" }`.
- AK-2: after remembering two setups as "Work" and "Private", `list.accounts` is both, in that order.
- AK-3: a setup with no `.credentials.json` (and a second case: `.credentials.json` without `claudeAiOauth`) is refused with `ClaudeAccountError` reason `notLoggedIn`; `list.accounts` is unchanged.
- AK-4: remembering bob's setup as "Work" (and as " work ") is refused with reason `nameInUse`; `list.accounts` still holds exactly `{ name: "Work", email: "alice@example.com" }`.
- Remembering the same account (same `accountUuid` and `organizationUuid`) a second time under another name is refused with reason `alreadyRemembered`, naming the existing name.
- AK-5: two setups, two remembered accounts: `list.setups` shows setup one `active: { email: "alice@example.com", rememberedAs: "Work" }` and setup two `active: { email: "bob@example.com", rememberedAs: "Private" }`.
- AK-6: a setup with carol logged in and nothing remembered for carol shows `active: { email: "carol@example.com", rememberedAs: null }`.
- AK-7: with nothing remembered, `list.accounts` is `[]` and every configured Claude setup is still listed with its active account; a setup with nobody logged in is listed with `active: null`; a non-Claude instance (e.g. `driver: "codex"`) is not listed.
- AK-8: forget "Private" leaves `list.accounts` = `[Work]`.
- AK-9: forget "Work" while alice is logged in on setup one: `list.accounts` is `[]`, and both `<tmp>/.credentials.json` and `<tmp>/.claude.json` are byte-identical to before the call; `list.setups` still shows alice active with `rememberedAs: null`.
- Forgetting a name that is not remembered is refused with reason `accountNotFound`.
- AK-23: after remember, the secret `claude-accounts` exists in `<stateDir>/secrets/claude-accounts.bin` with file mode `0o600` in a `0o700` directory (same as every other T3 secret); a recursive walk of the whole temporary T3 base directory finds the fixture access token and refresh token in no file other than `claude-accounts.bin`.
- AK-24: `JSON.stringify(list)` contains neither fixture token, nor the substrings `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `claudeAiOauth`; the listed account objects have exactly the keys `name` and `email`.
- No error raised by the service carries login content: for every refusal above, `JSON.stringify(error)` and `error.message` contain no fixture token.
- AK-27/AK-28/AK-29: with `HostProcess.Platform` provided as `"darwin"` (and once as `"win32"`), `remember`, `list` and `forget` each fail with reason `unavailable` and message "Claude account switching is unavailable on this system. It is supported on Linux only."; after the failed `remember`, `<stateDir>/secrets/claude-accounts.bin` does not exist.
Boundaries doubled: `HostProcess.Platform` and `HostProcess.HomeDirectory` (host OS), and the setup files (fixture files in temp dirs standing in for what the Claude CLI writes); everything else real — `ServerSecretStore`, `ServerSettingsService.layerTest`, `FileSystem`, `Path`.
e2e:
- There is no e2e suite (guard rail). AK-9's last line ("a new turn … runs as alice@example.com") needs a real Claude CLI; it is proven at the lowest level that can prove it: the setup's two login files are byte-identical after forgetting, so the next turn reads the same login. Named as such in the hand-off.

### Design reference


### Implementation details
Module: `apps/server` (provider)
Files:
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts` — add `resolveClaudeSetupPaths`, the one place that knows where a setup keeps its login and its account file.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.test.ts` — unit tests for `resolveClaudeSetupPaths`.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts` — replace the inline `configDir`/`accountConfigPath` computation (lines 158–163) with `resolveClaudeSetupPaths(effectiveConfig, processEnv)`; behaviour unchanged.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts` — delete the `claudeAccountConfigPath` export, whose only importer was ClaudeDriver (Knip fails CI on an unused export).
- [NEW] `apps/server/src/provider/claudeLoginFiles.ts` — read a setup's current Claude login and account identity from its two files.
- [NEW] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts` — the `ClaudeAccounts` service: remember, list, forget, Linux gate, storage in `ServerSecretStore`.
- [NEW] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts` — the integration tests above.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/server.ts` — add `ClaudeAccounts.layer` to the `Layer.mergeAll(...)` list of `layerRuntimeCoreDependenciesBase` next to `ProviderUsageLimitsIngestion.layer` (server.ts:601), where `layerServerSettings` and `ServerSecretStore.layer` are provided below it.

Consumes: nothing from earlier tickets. Existing: `ServerSecretStore.ServerSecretStore` (`get`, `set`), `ServerSettingsService` (`getSettings`), `deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap` (ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts), `ClaudeSettings` (`@t3tools/contracts`), `mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment` (`@t3tools/provider-core/server/instanceEnvironment`), `resolveClaudeHomePath`, `HostProcess.Platform`, `HostProcess.HomeDirectory`.

Produces (names used letter for letter by tickets 2 and 3):
- In `ClaudeHome.ts`:
  ```ts
  export interface ClaudeSetupPaths {
    readonly configDir: string;          // holds .credentials.json
    readonly accountConfigPath: string;  // the .claude.json holding oauthAccount
  }
  export const resolveClaudeSetupPaths: (
    config: Pick<ClaudeSettings, "homePath">,
    environment?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,
  ) => Effect.Effect<ClaudeSetupPaths, never, Path.Path>;
  ```
  `configDir = resolveClaudeHomePath(config, environment)`; `accountConfigPath = <configDir>/.claude.json` when `config.homePath.trim()` or `environment?.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR?.trim()` is non-empty, else `<HostProcess.HomeDirectory>/.claude.json` — exactly the rule ClaudeDriver applies today, because the Claude CLI keeps `.claude.json` beside `~/.claude`, not inside it, when no config dir is set.
- In `claudeLoginFiles.ts`:
  ```ts
  export type JsonObject = { readonly [key: string]: unknown };
  export interface ClaudeSetupLogin {
    readonly claudeAiOauth: JsonObject;  // the whole value under "claudeAiOauth" in .credentials.json, kept verbatim
    readonly oauthAccount: JsonObject;   // the whole value under "oauthAccount" in .claude.json, kept verbatim
    readonly identity: ClaudeAccountIdentity;
  }
  export interface ClaudeAccountIdentity {
    readonly email: string;                     // oauthAccount.emailAddress
    readonly accountUuid: string;               // oauthAccount.accountUuid
    readonly organizationUuid: string | null;   // oauthAccount.organizationUuid, null when absent
  }
  export const sameClaudeAccount: (a: ClaudeAccountIdentity, b: ClaudeAccountIdentity) => boolean; // accountUuid and organizationUuid equal
  export const readClaudeSetupLogin: (
    paths: ClaudeSetupPaths,
  ) => Effect.Effect<Option.Option<ClaudeSetupLogin>, ClaudeLoginFileError, FileSystem.FileSystem>;
  export class ClaudeLoginFileError extends Schema.TaggedError<ClaudeLoginFileError>()("ClaudeLoginFileError", {
    path: Schema.String,
  }) { override get message() { return `Could not read the Claude login file ${this.path}.`; } }
  ```
  `readClaudeSetupLogin` returns `Option.none()` ("not logged in") when `.credentials.json` is missing, has no object `claudeAiOauth`, or that object has no non-empty string `accessToken`; or when `.claude.json` is missing or its `oauthAccount` lacks a non-empty string `emailAddress` or `accountUuid`. It fails with `ClaudeLoginFileError` only when a file exists but cannot be read or is not a JSON object. The error deliberately carries only the path and never the parse cause, because Schema/JSON parse issues can quote the file's content. Values are decoded with `Schema.fromJsonString(Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Unknown))` so every key round-trips unchanged for ticket 2's write-back.
- In `ClaudeAccounts.ts`:
  ```ts
  export type ClaudeAccountErrorReason =
    | "unavailable" | "setupNotFound" | "setupUnreadable" | "notLoggedIn"
    | "invalidName" | "nameInUse" | "alreadyRemembered" | "accountNotFound" | "storage";
  export class ClaudeAccountError extends Schema.TaggedError<ClaudeAccountError>()("ClaudeAccountError", {
    reason: Schema.Literals([...]),
    instanceId: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
    name: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  }) { override get message(): string { /* per reason, table below */ } }

  export interface RememberedClaudeAccount { readonly name: string; readonly email: string }
  export interface ClaudeSetupAccountState {
    readonly instanceId: ProviderInstanceId;
    readonly displayName: string | undefined;
    readonly active: { readonly email: string; readonly rememberedAs: string | null } | null;
  }
  export interface ClaudeAccountList {
    readonly accounts: ReadonlyArray<RememberedClaudeAccount>;
    readonly setups: ReadonlyArray<ClaudeSetupAccountState>;
  }

  export class ClaudeAccounts extends Context.Service<ClaudeAccounts, {
    readonly remember: (input: { readonly instanceId: ProviderInstanceId; readonly name: string })
      => Effect.Effect<RememberedClaudeAccount, ClaudeAccountError>;
    readonly list: Effect.Effect<ClaudeAccountList, ClaudeAccountError>;
    readonly forget: (input: { readonly name: string }) => Effect.Effect<void, ClaudeAccountError>;
  }>()("t3/provider/ClaudeAccounts") {}
  export const layer: Layer.Layer<ClaudeAccounts, never,
    ServerSecretStore.ServerSecretStore | ServerSettingsService | FileSystem.FileSystem | Path.Path>;
  ```
  Ticket 2 adds `switch` to this same service and reuses its private helpers `resolveSetup(instanceId) → { instanceId, displayName, paths: ClaudeSetupPaths }`, `loadAccounts`, `saveAccounts` and the `accountsLock` semaphore — keep them as named functions inside `make`.

Error messages (`ClaudeAccountError.message`), user-readable and free of login content:
| reason | message |
|---|---|
| `unavailable` | Claude account switching is unavailable on this system. It is supported on Linux only. |
| `setupNotFound` | No Claude setup "<instanceId>" is configured. |
| `setupUnreadable` | Could not read the Claude login of setup "<instanceId>". |
| `notLoggedIn` | No Claude account is logged in on setup "<instanceId>". |
| `invalidName` | An account name must be 1 to 64 characters long. |
| `nameInUse` | The name "<name>" is already in use. |
| `alreadyRemembered` | This account is already remembered as "<name>". |
| `accountNotFound` | No remembered Claude account is named "<name>". |
| `storage` | Could not read or save the remembered Claude accounts. |

Behaviour:
- **Linux gate.** Every method first reads `HostProcess.Platform`; anything but `"linux"` fails with reason `unavailable` before any file or secret is read or written.
- **Setups.** `resolveSetup(instanceId)`: take `deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap(yield* settings.getSettings)`, pick the entry for `instanceId`; missing or `driver !== "claudeAgent"` → `setupNotFound`. Decode `entry.config ?? {}` with `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(ClaudeSettings)` (a config that fails to decode → `setupUnreadable`), merge `entry.environment` with `mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment`, then `resolveClaudeSetupPaths(config, env)`. `displayName` is `entry.displayName`. `list` uses every entry with `driver === "claudeAgent"`, in map order. Settings read failures map to `storage`.
- **Storage.** One secret named `claude-accounts`, value UTF-8 JSON `{ "version": 1, "accounts": [{ "name": string, "oauthAccount": object, "claudeAiOauth": object }] }`, decoded with a Schema; a missing secret is the empty list. Any `SecretStoreError`, or a stored value that does not decode, fails with reason `storage` and no cause attached (the decode issue would quote the stored login). `remember` and `forget` run their read-modify-write inside `accountsLock` (`Semaphore.make(1)`) and write with `ServerSecretStore.set`, which is atomic and `0o600`.
- **remember.** Gate → `resolveSetup` → `readClaudeSetupLogin(paths)` (`ClaudeLoginFileError` → `setupUnreadable`; `None` → `notLoggedIn`) → under the lock: name is trimmed, 1–64 characters (`invalidName` otherwise); a stored name equal ignoring case → `nameInUse`; a stored record with `sameClaudeAccount` → `alreadyRemembered` with that record's name; else append `{ name, oauthAccount, claudeAiOauth }` and save. Returns `{ name, email }`.
- **list.** Gate → load accounts → for each Claude setup, `readClaudeSetupLogin`; `None` or `ClaudeLoginFileError` → `active: null` (one unreadable setup must not hide the others); otherwise `active.email` from the identity and `rememberedAs` = name of the stored record with `sameClaudeAccount`, else `null`. `accounts` lists `{ name, email: oauthAccount.emailAddress }` in stored order. The result never contains `claudeAiOauth`.
- **forget.** Gate → under the lock: find the record by trimmed name ignoring case (`accountNotFound` otherwise), remove it, save. Never reads or writes any setup file.
- **Logging.** The service logs nothing that contains a record, a file's content or a `claudeAiOauth` value; a failed storage write may log `{ reason }` only.

Decisions:
- One secret holding the whole list, not one secret per account — `remember`/`forget` become one atomic `ServerSecretStore.set`, and listing needs no directory scan of the secrets folder (`ServerSecretStore` has no list method) — gives up per-account files, so the whole list is rewritten on every change (a handful of small records).
- Setup paths come from server settings (`deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap` + `ClaudeSettings`), not from a new service in `ClaudeDriverEnv` — no ripple into the many harnesses that build drivers — gives up reading the live driver's own resolved values; `resolveClaudeSetupPaths` keeps both on one rule so they cannot drift.
- Read the identity from `.claude.json` (`oauthAccount`) instead of the provider snapshot's probed email — no CLI spawn, works for a setup that is not running, and `oauthAccount` is exactly what ticket 2 must swap — gives up nothing the Auftrag needs; the snapshot remains the UI's live source.
- An account is the pair (`accountUuid`, `organizationUuid`), shown by email — one person in two organizations has two different logins — gives up treating them as one account.
- One `ClaudeAccountError` with a `reason` literal, not `ProviderSetupError` — `forget` and `list` have no single `instanceId`, and callers (tests, the later frontend) branch on the reason — gives up reuse of the existing provider setup error.
- Wire `ClaudeAccounts.layer` into `server.ts` now — the service is part of the running server and tickets 2–3 only extend it — gives up nothing; nothing calls it until a transport is added.

Deliberately left out: contracts, WS RPC methods, MCP tools and permission scopes for these actions — the Auftrag says the frontend Auftrag decides how they are triggered; renaming a remembered account; macOS keychain support (unavailable on non-Linux by requirement).
Deliberately added: refusing to remember the same account twice under two names (`alreadyRemembered`) — otherwise "active as <name>" in the list (R2) would be ambiguous; the `resolveClaudeSetupPaths` extraction — the switch in ticket 2 must write exactly the files the driver reads.

Behaviour:
- **Linux gate.** Every method first reads `HostProcess.Platform`; anything but `"linux"` fails with reason `unavailable` before any file or secret is read or written.
- **Setups.** `resolveSetup(instanceId)`: take `deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap(yield* settings.getSettings)`, pick the entry for `instanceId`; missing or `driver !== "claudeAgent"` → `setupNotFound`. Decode `entry.config ?? {}` with `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(ClaudeSettings)` (a config that fails to decode → `setupUnreadable`), merge `entry.environment` with `mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment`, then `resolveClaudeSetupPaths(config, env)`. `displayName` is `entry.displayName`. `list` uses every entry with `driver === "claudeAgent"`, in map order. Settings read failures map to `storage`.
- **Storage.** One secret named `claude-accounts`, value UTF-8 JSON `{ "version": 1, "accounts": [{ "name": string, "oauthAccount": object, "claudeAiOauth": object }] }`, decoded with a Schema; a missing secret is the empty list. Any `SecretStoreError`, or a stored value that does not decode, fails with reason `storage` and no cause attached (the decode issue would quote the stored login). `remember` and `forget` run their read-modify-write inside `accountsLock` (`Semaphore.make(1)`) and write with `ServerSecretStore.set`, which is atomic and `0o600`.
- **remember.** Gate → `resolveSetup` → `readClaudeSetupLogin(paths)` (`ClaudeLoginFileError` → `setupUnreadable`; `None` → `notLoggedIn`) → under the lock: name is trimmed, 1–64 characters (`invalidName` otherwise); a stored name equal ignoring case → `nameInUse`; a stored record with `sameClaudeAccount` → `alreadyRemembered` with that record's name; else append `{ name, oauthAccount, claudeAiOauth }` and save. Returns `{ name, email }`.
- **list.** Gate → load accounts → for each Claude setup, `readClaudeSetupLogin`; `None` or `ClaudeLoginFileError` → `active: null` (one unreadable setup must not hide the others); otherwise `active.email` from the identity and `rememberedAs` = name of the stored record with `sameClaudeAccount`, else `null`. `accounts` lists `{ name, email: oauthAccount.emailAddress }` in stored order. The result never contains `claudeAiOauth`.
- **forget.** Gate → under the lock: find the record by trimmed name ignoring case (`accountNotFound` otherwise), remove it, save. Never reads or writes any setup file.
- **Logging.** The service logs nothing that contains a record, a file's content or a `claudeAiOauth` value; a failed storage write may log `{ reason }` only.

Decisions:
- One secret holding the whole list, not one secret per account — `remember`/`forget` become one atomic `ServerSecretStore.set`, and listing needs no directory scan of the secrets folder (`ServerSecretStore` has no list method) — gives up per-account files, so the whole list is rewritten on every change (a handful of small records).
- Setup paths come from server settings (`deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap` + `ClaudeSettings`), not from a new service in `ClaudeDriverEnv` — no ripple into the many harnesses that build drivers — gives up reading the live driver's own resolved values; `resolveClaudeSetupPaths` keeps both on one rule so they cannot drift.
- Read the identity from `.claude.json` (`oauthAccount`) instead of the provider snapshot's probed email — no CLI spawn, works for a setup that is not running, and `oauthAccount` is exactly what ticket 2 must swap — gives up nothing the Auftrag needs; the snapshot remains the UI's live source.
- An account is the pair (`accountUuid`, `organizationUuid`), shown by email — one person in two organizations has two different logins — gives up treating them as one account.
- One `ClaudeAccountError` with a `reason` literal, not `ProviderSetupError` — `forget` and `list` have no single `instanceId`, and callers (tests, the later frontend) branch on the reason — gives up reuse of the existing provider setup error.
- Wire `ClaudeAccounts.layer` into `server.ts` now — the service is part of the running server and tickets 2–3 only extend it — gives up nothing; nothing calls it until a transport is added.

Deliberately left out: contracts, WS RPC methods, MCP tools and permission scopes for these actions — the Auftrag says the frontend Auftrag decides how they are triggered; renaming a remembered account; macOS keychain support (unavailable on non-Linux by requirement).
Deliberately added: refusing to remember the same account twice under two names (`alreadyRemembered`) — otherwise "active as <name>" in the list (R2) would be ambiguous; the `resolveClaudeSetupPaths` extraction — the switch in ticket 2 must write exactly the files the driver reads.

# Ticket 1 — Remember, list and forget Claude accounts — Round 2

### Blocked by

### Description
T3 can remember the Claude account that is currently logged in on one of its Claude setups, under a name the user chooses, show which accounts it remembers and which account is active on each Claude setup, and forget a remembered account again. Several accounts can be remembered per machine. The remembered login is kept in T3's own secret storage with the same protection as T3's other secrets and never appears in a listing, an error, or a log. Forgetting never touches a setup: an account that is still logged in stays logged in.

This ticket builds the backend service only. Nothing calls it from a client yet (a later frontend Auftrag does that), and switching between accounts is ticket 2 and ticket 3. On any system other than Linux, all three actions answer that they are unavailable.

A "Claude setup" is a configured Claude provider instance (driver kind `claudeAgent`), addressed by its `ProviderInstanceId`.

### Test specification
All tests use setups whose Claude config directory is a temporary directory the test creates and removes; no test reads or writes `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json` or `~/.t3` (guard rail). The setup temp dirs are created outside the `ServerConfig.layerTest` base dir. Each setup is declared through `ServerSettingsService.layerTest({ providerInstances: { <id>: { driver: "claudeAgent", config: { homePath: <tmp dir> } } } })`. Every integration test declares the id `claudeAgent` itself: "setup one" is `claudeAgent` and further setups use ids like `claudeWork2`. Otherwise `deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap` adds a default `claudeAgent` entry with an empty `homePath`, which would resolve to the real `~/.claude` (ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts:41). The integration layer also provides `HostProcess.HomeDirectory` as a fresh temp dir and `HostProcess.Environment` without `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so no fallback can reach a real directory. Every `list.setups` assertion compares the exact ordered array of `instanceId`s the test declared. and its login is written by the test as two fixture files: `<tmp>/.credentials.json` = `{ "claudeAiOauth": { "accessToken": "<unique token>", "refreshToken": "<unique token>", "expiresAt": <ms>, "scopes": ["user:inference"] }, "mcpOAuth": { … } }` and `<tmp>/.claude.json` = `{ "oauthAccount": { "emailAddress": "alice@example.com", "accountUuid": "<uuid>", "organizationUuid": "<uuid>" }, "numStartups": 3, "projects": { … } }`. Token fixture values are unique random strings so a leak search cannot match by accident.

# Ticket 2 — Switch a Claude setup to another remembered account — Round 1

### Description
T3 can switch a Claude setup to another account it remembers. Before switching, T3 refuses when the switch would be unsafe or impossible: on any system other than Linux, when the account currently logged in on the setup is not remembered (its login would be lost), when Claude programs started outside T3 are using the setup (they would overwrite the switch or be broken by it), and when the saved login of the target account no longer works (the user is told that this account needs a fresh login). When none of these apply, T3 first saves the latest login of the outgoing account, so switching back later works without logging in again, and then replaces only the logged-in Claude account in the setup's files. Everything else the setup holds (settings, history, logins for other services) stays as it was. If the change fails partway, T3 puts the setup back exactly as it was and reports the failure.

This ticket adds `switch` to the `ClaudeAccounts` service built in ticket 1 (#3), plus the two pieces it needs: the check for Claude programs outside T3, and the check of a saved login. Stopping T3's own running turns on the setup before the files change, refreshing the setup's "who is logged in" label afterwards, and wiring the service into the running server are ticket 3. Nothing calls `switch` from a client yet.

A "Claude setup" is a configured Claude provider instance (driver kind `claudeAgent`), addressed by its `ProviderInstanceId`.

- The login check lets the Claude CLI itself use the saved login, in a throwaway config dir, through the existing `probeClaudeCapabilities` usage request. The alternative was calling Anthropic's OAuth token or usage endpoints from T3. A saved login is usually past its short-lived access token, so only a renewal proves it still works, and the CLI renews with its own client details, which T3 does not have and should not copy. The CLI writes the renewed login into the temp dir, and T3 keeps that copy. What this gives up: about one CLI start per switch (bounded by the probe's 25 s timeout), and a usage request that fails for a network reason reports `needsFreshLogin` instead of `loginCheckFailed`. That error is safe: the switch is refused and nothing changes.
- The renewed target login is saved to the remembered record before the setup files are written, and that save is not undone when the file write fails. Renewing rotates the refresh token, so the old stored copy is dead the moment the check succeeds. What this gives up: after a failed switch, the record differs from what was stored before the call, which the AK-19 test pins down.
- "Outside T3" is decided by an environment marker (`T3CODE_CLAUDE_OWNER_PID=<server pid>`) that T3 sets on every Claude CLI it spawns, not by process ancestry or the agent cgroup slice. systemd scopes are not descendants of the server, and without systemd the user's terminals are descendants. The marker is exact in both cases, and a `claude` the user starts in a T3 terminal is correctly "outside T3", because terminal/Manager.ts is deliberately not changed. What this gives up: the four spawn sites must keep applying the marker; docs/internals/providers.md records that.
- Config dirs are compared with `path.resolve`, not `realpath`. What this gives up: a Claude program that reaches the same directory through a symlinked path is not detected.
- The setup files are written with an own keep-mode atomic write, not `writeFileStringAtomically`. That helper creates the new file with the default mode (typically `0o644`), which would expose `.credentials.json` to other local users.
- `.credentials.json` is written before `.claude.json`, with a rollback of the first write. Two files cannot be renamed atomically together, so "never half-switched" is reached by restoring. What this gives up: during the few milliseconds between the two renames, a reader could see the new login with the old identity. T3's readers run under `accountsLock` or tolerate it (`list` is read-only), and external programs are refused.
- The whole switch runs under ticket 1's `accountsLock`, not a per-setup lock. A concurrent `remember` would otherwise read a half-written pair. What this gives up: switches on different setups, and remember/forget, wait for each other (including the login check's CLI start).
- `ResetCreditCoordinator` is not taken. Reset credits only read the access token, and each file is replaced atomically, so they see the old or the new login, both valid.
- Switching a setup on which nobody is logged in is refused with `notLoggedIn`. There is no outgoing login to save, and the files may not exist.
- Switching to the account already active succeeds without doing anything, instead of being refused. The caller asked for a state that already holds.

**Where:** ticket §Implementation details, "ClaudeLoginCheck (live)" (temp dir read back only when `usage` is present) and "applySwitch" step 1 (`switchFailed`, "with nothing written"); §Decisions, "Renewing rotates the refresh token, so the old stored copy is dead the moment the check succeeds"

**Why:** the refresh-token rotation is a mutation at Anthropic that has already happened, but the ticket keeps its result only on `Valid` followed by a successful step-2 save; on `NeedsLogin`/`Unknown` after a renewal, on a step-1 `switchFailed` (the "setup changes during the check" test), and on any failure ticket 3 inserts between `checkSwitch` and `applySwitch`, the temp dir is deleted and the stored record keeps a refresh token that is now dead — so a refused or failed switch silently breaks the remembered account it was asked to protect.

# Ticket 2 — Switch a Claude setup to another remembered account — Round 2

### Blocked by
#3

### Description
T3 can switch a Claude setup to another account it remembers. Before switching, T3 refuses and changes nothing in these cases:
- on any system other than Linux;
- when the account currently logged in on the setup is not remembered, because its login would be lost;
- when the saved login of the target account no longer works; the user is told that this account needs a fresh login.

When none of these apply, T3 first saves the latest login of the outgoing account, so that switching back later works without logging in again. It then replaces only the logged-in Claude account in the setup's files. Everything else the setup holds (settings, history, logins for other services) stays as it was. If the change fails partway, T3 puts the setup back exactly as it was and reports the failure.

The login belongs to the setup's Claude config directory, so every Claude setup configured on the same directory is switched together, and the result names all of them.

This ticket adds `switch` to the `ClaudeAccounts` service built in ticket 1 (#3), and adds the check of a saved login that `switch` needs. Later tickets cover the rest:
- **Ticket 3:** the refusal when Claude programs outside T3 use the setup (AK-20).
- **Ticket 4:**
  - stopping T3's own running turns on the affected setups before the files change;
  - refreshing their "who is logged in" label afterwards;
  - wiring the services into the running server.

Nothing calls `switch` from a client yet.

A "Claude setup" is a configured Claude provider instance (driver kind `claudeAgent`), addressed by its `ProviderInstanceId`.

Decisions:
- **How a saved login is checked.**
  - The login check lets the Claude CLI itself use the saved login, in a throwaway config dir, through the existing `probeClaudeCapabilities` usage request. The alternative was calling Anthropic's OAuth token or usage endpoints from T3.
  - Why: a saved login is usually past its short-lived access token, so only a renewal proves it still works. The CLI renews with its own client details, which T3 does not have and should not copy.
  - Cost: one CLI start per switch, up to about 29 s.
  - A failed usage request on a login whose access token is fresh counts as `Unknown`, not `NeedsLogin`, so a network problem does not send the user through a needless fresh login.
- **Renewals are saved at once.** Any login the CLI leaves in the throwaway dir is saved to the target's record right after the check, on every path. The check's renewal rotates the refresh token at Anthropic, so the previously stored copy is dead from that moment. Cost: after a refused or failed switch, the target record differs from what was stored before the call; the tests pin this down.
- **Setups that share a config dir are switched together.** All Claude setups on the same config dir switch together and are reported in `affectedInstanceIds`, instead of the switch being refused or acting on one instance only. They share one login file (facts #23, #101), so a per-instance switch is impossible, and refusing would make a shared directory unswitchable. Cost: switching one setup changes its siblings. The result names them, and ticket 4 stops all of them.
- **The shared atomic write is extended.** `writeFileStringAtomically` gains an optional `mode` instead of getting a second atomic-write implementation. Its default (no mode) creates the file at `0o644`, which would expose `.credentials.json`. `.credentials.json` is always written at `originalMode & 0o600`, so a setup that had a too-wide mode gets narrowed rather than carrying it over to another account's token.
- **Two files, restored on failure.** `.credentials.json` is written before `.claude.json`, and the first write is rolled back if the second fails. Two files cannot be renamed atomically together, so "never half-switched" is reached by restoring. Cost: for the milliseconds between the two renames, a reader could see the new login with the old identity. T3's own readers run under `accountsLock` or tolerate it (`list` is read-only).
- **Re-serialising the JSON files.** `.claude.json` and `.credentials.json` are re-serialised with `JSON.stringify(…, null, 2)`. Every other key keeps its value and position, but formatting, duplicate keys and integers above 2^53 are not preserved byte for byte. This is accepted: the Claude CLI rewrites these files the same way on every save, so their formatting is not an invariant anyone holds. The tests assert deep equality.
- **One lock for the whole switch.** The whole switch runs under ticket 1's `accountsLock`, not a per-setup lock, because a concurrent `remember` would otherwise read a half-written pair. Cost: switches on different setups, and remember/forget, wait for each other, including the login check's CLI start.
- **`ResetCreditCoordinator` is not taken.** Reset credits only read the access token, and each file is replaced atomically, so they see the old or the new login, both valid.
- **A setup with no login cannot be switched.** Switching a setup on which nobody is logged in is refused with `notLoggedIn`: there is no outgoing login to save, and the files may not exist.
- **Switching to the active account is a no-op.** It succeeds without doing anything, instead of running the check and rewriting the same login. The alternative path would spend a CLI start and, after ticket 4, stop the setup's sessions for nothing; the no-op is one comparison.
- **The throwaway dir stays in the OS temp dir.** It is not placed under T3's state dir, which is kept free of plain logins (AK-23). `mkdtemp`'s `0o700` limits it to the same user, who already holds the setup's login files in plain form. Cost: a server crash during the check leaves the dir until the OS cleans its temp dir.

# Ticket 3 — Refuse a switch while Claude programs outside T3 use the setup — Round 1

### Blocked by
#4

### Description
A switch rewrites the login files of a Claude setup's config directory. A Claude program started outside T3 that uses the same directory would overwrite the switch, or break because of it. So T3 refuses the switch while such a program runs, says why, and changes nothing.

"Outside T3" means: not spawned by this T3 server. T3 marks every Claude CLI it spawns itself (provider turns, capability probes, `claude --version` checks, text generation). That way the check can tell its own programs apart from the rest. A `claude` the user starts by hand counts as outside T3, including one started in a T3 terminal. So does a `claude` run by another T3 server.

The check reads `/proc` only. It never signals or stops any process. It runs twice: before the saved login of the target account is checked, and again right before the files change. A program started outside T3 while the up-to-29 s login check runs is caught too.

This ticket adds that gate to `ClaudeAccounts.switch` from ticket 2 (#4). Ticket 4 stops T3's own sessions and wires the services into the server.

# Ticket 3 — Refuse a switch while Claude programs outside T3 use the setup — Round 1

### Blocked by
#4

### Description
A switch rewrites the login files of a Claude setup's config directory. A Claude program started outside T3 that uses the same directory would overwrite the switch, or break because of it. So T3 refuses the switch while such a program runs, says why, and changes nothing.

"Outside T3" means: not spawned by this T3 server. T3 marks every Claude CLI it spawns itself (provider turns, capability probes, `claude --version` checks, text generation). That way the check can tell its own programs apart from the rest. A `claude` the user starts by hand counts as outside T3, including one started in a T3 terminal. So does a `claude` run by another T3 server.

The check reads `/proc` only. It never signals or stops any process. It runs twice: before the saved login of the target account is checked, and again right before the files change. A program started outside T3 while the up-to-29 s login check runs is caught too.

This ticket adds that gate to `ClaudeAccounts.switch` from ticket 2 (#4). Ticket 4 stops T3's own sessions and wires the services into the server.

- **An environment marker, not ancestry or cgroup.** "Spawned by this T3 server" is decided by `T3CODE_CLAUDE_OWNER_PID=<server pid>` in the program's environment, not by process ancestry or the agent cgroup slice.

  - Cost: a process the T3 CLI itself starts (a `claude` run by an agent's shell tool) inherits the marker and counts as T3's. It usually lives in T3's own session, which ticket 4 stops; one detached with `setsid`/`nohup` outside a systemd scope may outlive that stop and still pass the gate.
  - Trust level: the marker is a cooperative tag, not a proof of origin. The pid is not secret, so any process of the same user can set it. Forging it gains nothing: the same user can rewrite the login files directly. No other control may be built on it (security-1).
- **The marker sits in the one constructor.** It sits in `makeClaudeEnvironment`, which every T3 spawn site already calls, and terminals get a separately named unmarked variant (architect-3, carried).
  - Why: a fifth spawn site that copies today's pattern is marked automatically, and opting out is an explicit, named call.
  - Cost: `makeClaudeEnvironment` no longer returns its input object when `homePath` is empty, and the line-26 identity assertion changes. Nothing else relies on that identity. - **The server pid comes from one reference.** It comes from `HostProcess.ProcessId`, read by both the marker writer and the scanner (architect-4, carried).
  - Why: both sides cannot diverge, and tests pin the pid.
  - Cost: one new export in `packages/shared`, in the same form as its siblings.

# Concurrency — Ticket 4: Switching stops the setup's T3 sessions; threads continue on the new account — Round 1

## Findings

**[blocker] concurrency-1 — Turns admitted during the stop are neither gated nor named; a queued run starts on the old login and then fails**
**Where:** ticket §Implementation details, `stopSetupSessions` steps 2–4; §Deliberately left out, "A turn started between the stop and the file write … normally milliseconds"
**Evidence:** step 2 enumerates threads once, then steps 3–4 act on that snapshot. Step 3's `interruptThread` call passes no `holdQueue`. `run.interrupt` takes `holdQueue?` (fact #117). Without it, Orchestrator.ts:9541 takes the `disposeDelegatedCompletionCohort` branch, not `holdStoppedThread`, so the thread's queued runs stay queued. Releasing a session mid-turn fails the run (fact #123), and `open` picks up the adapter at turn start (fact #130).
**Why:** a message queued behind the interrupted run, or a new message sent during the wait of up to 10 s, starts a turn on the outgoing login after enumeration. `closeInstance` then releases it mid-turn, so it ends `failed`, the outcome AK-13 rules out. If the turn opens after `closeInstance`, it holds the old tokens while the files change, the state R8 forbids. This check-then-act window is the whole stop, up to `CLAUDE_SWITCH_STOP_TIMEOUT`. It is not the millisecond window the ticket accepts.
**Closes when:** the ticket says how a run admitted on an affected instance between enumeration and `applySwitch` is kept out: `holdQueue: true` on the interrupt, re-enumeration after `closeInstance` that refuses on any new active run, or an admission gate. Alternatively, it accepts this wider window explicitly with its outcome (`failed`). The test specification adds a scenario where a second run is queued on the thread with the held turn, and asserts the named outcome.

**[blocker] concurrency-2 — No scenario has a second actor start work on the setup during a switch**
**Where:** ticket §Test specification, Integration list
**Evidence:** every scenario fixes the thread state before calling `switch` and changes nothing while the stop runs. The only concurrent-looking case, two instances on one config dir, is a fixed precondition too.
**Why:** the stop step's correctness depends on what it does with a turn that starts while it runs (concurrency-1). No test has a second actor do that, so timing, not a named mechanism, decides the result.
**Closes when:** at least one scenario starts or queues a turn on the affected instance while the switch is inside the stop step (sequenced on the fake adapter's `interruptTurn` `Deferred`, not by sleeping) and asserts the outcome the ticket names for it.

**[suggestion] concurrency-3 — An in-flight capability probe can write the old account back into the cache after `invalidateCaches`**
**Where:** ticket §Implementation details, `switch` step 4 and Decision "Cache invalidation, not a forced refresh"
**Evidence:** `refreshSetups` runs once, after `applySwitch`. Nothing orders it against a probe that started before the file write and finishes after the invalidation.
**Why:** that probe stores the outgoing account's result after the cache was dropped, so the snapshot shows the old email until the next invalidation.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket states whether a probe started before the write may repopulate the cache afterwards, and either accepts it or names the ordering, e.g. a generation check in the cache.

## Out of lens
gremium-reliability: `Effect.timeout` over the stop interrupts the fiber mid-way. Interrupts already dispatched still persist, and the ticket says only "turns already interrupted stay interrupted", not what happens to sessions `closeInstance` had only partly released.
Round 1:  2 blockers, 1 suggestion. Turns admitted on the setup while the stop runs have no named resolution and no concurrent test.

# Fixes — Ticket 4: Switching stops the setup's T3 sessions — Round 2

Four blockers answered. Suggestions are answered in the ruling. No plan amendment.

### concurrency-1
Fix: `stopSetupSessions` dispatches `{ type: "run.interrupt", commandId, threadId, runId, reason: "Claude account switched", holdQueue: true }` through `ThreadManagementService.dispatch` (contracts orchestrationV2.ts:2867) instead of `interruptThread`, so queued runs stay held and do not start on the outgoing login. After the interrupt wait it enumerates once more and interrupts and awaits, the same way, any run that became active on an affected instance in the meantime, still under the one `CLAUDE_SWITCH_STOP_TIMEOUT`. Then `closeInstance`. Then a final check: any active run or any provider session not `stopped`/`error` on an affected instance → `sessionStopFailed`, nothing written.
After `applySwitch`, whether it succeeds or fails, and also after a `sessionStopFailed`, `switch` dispatches `{ type: "queue.resume", commandId, threadId }` for every thread it held, so held messages start on the login the setup holds then.
Named residual: a turn admitted in the milliseconds between the last enumeration and `closeInstance` is released mid-turn and ends `failed`. It is a turn started after the switch began, not one AK-13 covers. This goes into §Deliberately left out with that outcome.

### concurrency-2
Fix: new scenario "work admitted during the stop". Thread A on setup one has a held running turn and a second message queued behind it. Thread B on setup one is idle. The fake `interruptTurn` for A completes a `Deferred` and then waits on a second `Deferred`. The test forks `switch`, awaits the first `Deferred`, sends a message on B (held by the fake adapter), then releases the second.
Asserts: `switch` succeeds. A's first run and B's run are `interrupted`, not `failed`. A's queued run did not start before `switch` returned and completes afterwards on resumed queue, with its `openSession` index after the mark (see testability-4). Setup one's files hold Private.

### testability-1
Fix: the test-layer helper is `makeAccountsTestLayer(options)`. It is called inside each `it.effect` and provided with `Effect.provide(...)`, as `ThreadStop.test.ts` provides per test. It builds a fresh `SqlitePersistence.layerMemory`, registry, fake adapter records, invalidation `Ref` and `Deferred`s per test, under `Layer.fresh` where a layer reference would otherwise be memoized. No `it.layer` shares the orchestration stack. Tests that leave a turn held release its `Deferred` in a finalizer.

### testability-2
Fix: the stop-timeout test forks `switch` with `Effect.fork`. It awaits a `Deferred` that the fake `interruptTurn` completes when it is called and then ignores the interrupt. Then it runs `TestClock.adjust(Duration.sum(CLAUDE_SWITCH_STOP_TIMEOUT, Duration.seconds(1)))` and `Fiber.join`s the fiber, which fails with `sessionStopFailed`. The word "overridden" goes. `CLAUDE_SWITCH_STOP_TIMEOUT` stays an exported constant and is only read by the test.
